topic: What if Earth got a ring like Saturn tonight

through_line.name: the ring
through_line.progression: asteroid on approach, shredded into a stream, a thin bright band, a wide glowing arch, a black midnight gap, a dark shadow stripe on the ground, sparks as satellites strike it, streaks of falling debris, worn thin beside the Moon, gone
through_line.resolution: In the payoff the ring disk pulls itself together into the Moon and modern Earth is shown with no ring at all.

blocks.vo_line: Earth once had a ring. Four hundred sixty six million years ago a band of rock circled our planet and helped freeze it.
blocks.through_line_state: a dim complete band of rock around the equator
shots: WIDE, static: Earth hangs alone in dark space, stars drift, a pale band of rock snaps into place around the equator.
CU, slow push-in: the band's rocky grains tumble in a slow current, each pebble catching sunlight.
MEDIUM, overhead: the ancient continents below, twenty one dark dots stamp down one after another along a belt near the equator.
ECU, macro: frost crystals spread across a patch of ocean and lock it white.
WIDE, gentle drift: the ringed Earth rotates once, the band's shadow settles as a dark stripe across the south, then holds.

blocks.vo_line: Imagine it returns tonight, identical size and place, except now fourteen thousand satellites and eight billion people sit underneath it.
blocks.through_line_state: a faint pale line fading in over the city
shots: MEDIUM, low angle: Nia steps to the rooftop railing, city towers glowing behind her, and looks up.
WIDE, static: the equatorial skyline at night, tiny satellite lights crawl across the sky in staggered lines.
CU, slow push-in: Nia's eyes widen as a faint pale line fades in across the stars above.
ECU, macro: one satellite glides past, solar panels catching light, then a second, then a third.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: the whole rooftop tilts up toward the new line, Nia grips the rail as it settles bright.

blocks.vo_line: It begins with an asteroid roughly twelve kilometers across, comparable to the width of a sprawling city, and it never actually hits us.
blocks.through_line_state: not yet a ring, a lumpy asteroid on approach
shots: MEDIUM, lateral drift: a grey lumpy asteroid tumbles into frame from the right, trailing dust.
ECU, macro: pitted craters on its surface roll past, pebbles shake loose and drift.
WIDE, static: Earth small on the left, the asteroid's curved path arcs toward the planet and bends past its edge.
CU, slow push-in: the asteroid's leading face brightens as Earth's glow spills over it.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: the rock slides past Earth without touching, the gap between them shrinks and holds.

blocks.vo_line: Every planet has a line called the Roche limit, where gravity tugs the near side of an object harder than its far side.
blocks.through_line_state: a pale chalk circle drawn around a desk globe
shots: WIDE, static: the lab interior, Theo at a long desk with a desk globe, a big window showing a faint line in the sky.
CU, slow push-in: Theo's finger traces a chalk circle around the globe at a distance, the circle snaps closed.
MEDIUM, low angle: a small rubber ball on a string swings toward the globe and visibly stretches as it nears.
ECU, macro: the ball's near side bulges toward the globe while the far side lags behind.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Theo taps the chalk line twice, dust puffs, and the globe settles spinning slowly.

blocks.vo_line: For a rubble pile asteroid that boundary sits around eighteen thousand kilometers above the ground, and our visitor crosses it at full speed.
blocks.through_line_state: the asteroid touching the dashed boundary line
shots: CU, static: a dashed boundary circle glows around Earth, the asteroid's nose crosses it.
WIDE, slow push-in: the full arc of the path bends inside the dashed line, the rock accelerating along it.
ECU, macro: a crack races across the asteroid's surface with a sharp snap.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: the asteroid stretches long like taffy as it swings past the planet.
CU, gentle drift: two halves separate with a slow shudder and drift apart, then settle.

blocks.vo_line: The rock stretches and tears into billions of fragments that keep orbital speed, so nothing falls and everything spreads sideways.
blocks.through_line_state: fragments smearing into a curved stream
shots: MEDIUM, static: the two halves shatter into a spray of thousands of fragments, one burst then another.
ECU, macro: single pebbles fly sideways along the orbit, none of them dropping toward the planet.
WIDE, gentle drift: the spray stretches into a long curved stream that begins to wrap around Earth.
CU, slow push-in: the stream's leading edge meets its own tail and the loop closes.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: the closed loop of rubble thins and flattens into a plane, then holds.

blocks.vo_line: Within months the debris flattens into a disk over the equator, only ten meters thick, roughly the height of a three story building.
blocks.through_line_state: a thin bright band completing overhead
shots: WIDE, static: a small backyard at dusk, Nia on a lawn chair beside a telescope, the sky deepening.
CU, slow push-in: a thin band brightens across the sky above her, edge to edge, in one clean sweep.
ECU, macro: a side-on view of the band, drawn as a single hairline against the stars.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia stands, mouth open, the telescope tilting up beside her.
WIDE, gentle drift: the band's thinness beside the wide backyard, a three story house next door for scale, settles.

blocks.vo_line: Where you stand decides what you see, and on the equator the ring becomes a thin line straight overhead from east to west.
blocks.through_line_state: a thin line straight overhead through the zenith
shots: CU, low angle: straight up from the rooftop, the ring is a thin bright line running east to west through the zenith.
MEDIUM, static: Nia tilts her head fully back, hair falling, the line reflected in her glasses.
WIDE, gentle drift: the equatorial city under one thin line, like a laser drawn across the sky.
ECU, macro: the line's edge, tiny tumbling grains barely visible in a row.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: Nia raises a hand and lines up her thumb with the band, then lowers it as the frame settles.

blocks.vo_line: Travel north to forty one degrees latitude and the geometry changes, turning the ring into a wide glowing arch across the southern sky.
blocks.through_line_state: a wide glowing arch low in the southern sky
shots: WIDE, static: a snowy northern street at night, apartment blocks, a wide glowing arch low in the southern sky.
MEDIUM, low angle: Theo in a puffy coat steps out of a doorway and stops mid-step.
CU, slow push-in: his breath fogs as his eyes follow the arch from one rooftop to the other.
ECU, macro: the arch's inner edge, a soft glow spilling over snow on a car roof.
WIDE, gentle drift: the arch climbs higher than the Moon ever sits in winter, street lamps flicker, then hold.

blocks.vo_line: Past sixty degrees the arch sits low, and it glows all night because Saturn's rings reflect four times more sunlight than the Moon.
blocks.through_line_state: a low flat arch hugging the horizon
shots: WIDE, static: a frozen valley under a starry sky, the ring a low flat arch hugging the horizon.
CU, slow push-in: the arch's glow lays a pale stripe across the ice field.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: a split comparison, the small Moon rising on one side, the arch shining brighter on the other.
ECU, macro: reflected light glints in a crack in the ice, then brightens as the arch rises a little.
WIDE, gentle drift: the whole valley lit by ring light, shadows of ice blocks stretch long and settle.

blocks.vo_line: Earth's ring would be rubble and dust instead of ice, dimmer than Saturn's, yet bright enough to illuminate an entire night like moonlight.
blocks.through_line_state: a rocky band outside the window lighting the room
shots: MEDIUM, static: Theo sets two sample jars on the desk, one of grey grit, one of ice chips.
ECU, macro: the ice jar catches the lamp and flares bright, the grit jar glows softly.
CU, low angle: Theo slides the grit jar forward and taps it, dust settles inside.
WIDE, gentle drift: the lab window, the ring outside dimmer than a full Moon but lighting the room.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: Theo switches off the desk lamp and the room stays lit by the band outside, holds.

blocks.vo_line: There is one strange exception, since around midnight on the equator Earth's own shadow falls across the ring directly above your head.
blocks.through_line_state: a black bite eaten out of the ring overhead
shots: ECU, macro: a clock face on Nia's wrist ticks to midnight.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia looks straight up, the ring bright overhead.
WIDE, static: Earth's shadow drawn as a dark cone sweeping across the sky, swallowing the overhead segment.
CU, slow push-in: the ring directly above goes black while both horizons keep glowing.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia's face lit only from the sides, the dark gap holding overhead.

blocks.vo_line: The brightest object in the entire sky goes completely black overhead every single night, and yet the ring is not only above you.
blocks.through_line_state: the black gap at the top of the arc, its shadow on the streets
shots: MEDIUM, lateral drift: a side view along the rooftop railing, the ring arcing overhead with a dark bite at its top.
CU, static: Nia checks the time again, shrugs, and points down at the rooftop floor.
WIDE, high angle: from above the rooftop, the dark ring shadow crawling across the city streets below.
ECU, macro: the shadow's edge slides over a rooftop water tank.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: Nia steps into the shadow band on the roof and stops, settles.

blocks.vo_line: Earth is tilted twenty three point four degrees, which creates our seasons, and a ring above the equator never aligns with the Sun.
blocks.through_line_state: a paper ring around a tilted desk globe
shots: CU, static: Theo's hands tilt the desk globe over, a paper ring snapped around its middle.
MEDIUM, low angle: a desk lamp stands in for the Sun, the globe's tilt visible against its light.
ECU, macro: the paper ring's edge never lines up with the lamp, light cuts across it at an angle.
WIDE, gentle drift: the whole desk setup, globe orbiting the lamp on a slow turntable.
CU, slow push-in: the ring's shadow lands as a thin dark stripe on the globe's lower half, holds.

blocks.vo_line: In June the north leans toward the Sun, sunlight arrives from above the ring plane, and the shadow lands on the southern hemisphere.
blocks.through_line_state: a dark shadow stripe across the southern hemisphere
shots: MEDIUM, static: Earth tilted, sunlight pouring in from the upper left across the ring plane.
ECU, macro: light glances across the ring's top face, grains lighting one by one.
WIDE, slow push-in: the ring's shadow drops onto the southern hemisphere as a wide dark stripe.
CU, lateral drift: the stripe crossing an iced southern coastline.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: a small sun symbol stamps into the upper left corner of space, the stripe holding.

blocks.vo_line: Southern winter gets a second layer of darkness over the normal one, then in December everything flips and the north takes its turn.
blocks.through_line_state: the shadow stripe flipping to the north
shots: CU, static: Earth swings around the far side of its orbit, the tilt now pointing away.
WIDE, gentle drift: light arrives from below the ring plane, the dark stripe leaps to the northern hemisphere.
ECU, macro: the shadow edge crosses a snow covered coastline in the north.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: the southern stripe fades while the northern stripe darkens, one then the other.
CU, slow push-in: the northern stripe widens a little and holds.

blocks.vo_line: The shadow reaches widest and farthest from the equator exactly at the solstices, so deep winter also becomes the darkest stretch of shade.
blocks.through_line_state: a broad shadow band down the whole street
shots: MEDIUM, static: Theo shovels snow from a doorstep, the arch overhead casting a broad shadow band down the street.
ECU, macro: a thermometer's marker slides down, then down again.
CU, low angle: Theo pulls his scarf tighter and looks up at the band's edge.
WIDE, high angle: the street from above, the shadow band at its widest, streetlights on at midday.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: Theo plants the shovel, snow stops falling, the shadow holds.

blocks.vo_line: This is not a guess, because in two thousand twenty four a Monash University team examined twenty one craters from an ancient bombardment.
blocks.through_line_state: twenty one red dots in a belt on the desk globe
shots: CU, static: Theo presses a red dot onto the desk globe, then another, then a third.
WIDE, lateral drift: the reverse side of the lab, a wall screen showing the globe outline, dots stamping down one by one.
ECU, macro: a dot lands with a soft stamp right beside the equator line.
MEDIUM, low angle: Theo steps back and counts on his fingers, nodding.
CU, slow push-in: the completed cluster of dots on the globe, all in one belt, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Every crater sits within thirty degrees of the equator, though over seventy percent of continental crust lies outside that band.
blocks.through_line_state: the old ring bright over a shallow sea, shedding rocks
shots: WIDE, static: an ancient shallow sea coast, rounded strange plants, the old ring bright across the sky.
CU, slow push-in: a glowing fragment streaks down and slams into the shallows with a splash.
ECU, macro: a second impact ripple spreads through the water.
MEDIUM, high angle: from above the coastline, craters pocking the shore in a band, one then another.
WIDE, gentle drift: the belt of craters across the continent while the land far to the north stays untouched, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Random strikes never cluster like that, but ring fallout does, and late in that ring's life the planet slid into a deep freeze.
blocks.through_line_state: the old ring thinner, frost creeping under it
shots: MEDIUM, static: the shallow sea under the ring, another fragment falls, then the water goes still.
ECU, macro: frost crystals crawl across the surface of the water, locking it.
CU, low angle: the ring overhead, noticeably thinner, its shadow creeping across the beach.
WIDE, gentle drift: the shoreline freezing from the south, ice climbing the rocks.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: the frozen shallows under the thinning band, snow starts to fall, settles.

blocks.vo_line: The Hirnantian glaciation began four hundred forty five million years ago, among the coldest stretches in five hundred million years.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring a faint thread above deep ice
shots: CU, static: a wall of blue ice grinds forward, cracking.
WIDE, gentle drift: the valley buried under ice, the ring a faint thread above.
ECU, macro: a frozen fern trapped inside the ice.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: ice blocks tumble from the glacier face, one after another, splashing.
CU, slow push-in: the faint ring thread above the ice field, holds.

blocks.vo_line: A modern ring means colder longer winters in both hemispheres, and the debris overhead soon becomes a bigger problem than the cold.
blocks.through_line_state: the modern ring with the first streaks of falling debris
shots: MEDIUM, static: Theo scrapes ice from a car windshield in dim daylight, the ring band above.
ECU, macro: a bright streak crosses the sky and fades, then a second.
CU, low angle: Theo squints up as sparks flicker along the ring's inner edge.
WIDE, high angle: the street below, snow piled high, more streaks raining across the sky.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: Theo's scraper pauses mid stroke, a streak reflected in the glass, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Right now over fourteen thousand active satellites circle Earth, and most of them orbit five hundred kilometers up, which is inside the ring.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring slicing across a wall display of satellites
shots: WIDE, static: a control room, curved wall display of Earth ringed by thousands of tiny satellite dots.
CU, slow push-in: the ring drawn across the display slices straight through the lowest layer of dots.
MEDIUM, low angle: Theo at a console, hands hovering, staring at the display.
ECU, macro: a satellite model on the desk, solar panels folding out with a click.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: the display's dots clustering just above the surface, the ring band overlapping them, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Ring particles move near eight kilometers per second, and a satellite on a polar orbit crosses that ring plane twice every ninety minutes.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring plane with a satellite diving through it
shots: CU, static: a satellite races along a polar path, panels gleaming.
WIDE, lateral drift: the polar orbit drawn as a loop over both poles, crossing the flat ring twice.
ECU, macro: ring grains streaming sideways at speed, blurred.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: the satellite dips through the ring plane, grains whipping past it.
CU, gentle drift: it emerges on the far side, a panel scratched, and holds.

blocks.vo_line: A grain of sand at that speed hits like a bullet, a fist sized rock destroys a spacecraft, and internet constellations go first.
blocks.through_line_state: sparks along the ring where satellites strike it
shots: ECU, macro: a single grain of sand flies at the camera and snaps past.
MEDIUM, static: the grain punches a neat hole through a satellite panel with a spark.
CU, slow push-in: a fist sized rock tumbles in and the satellite bursts into pieces.
WIDE, gentle drift: a whole shell of tiny satellite lights flickers out one by one along the ring.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: debris joins the ring's stream, the band slightly thicker, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Weather satellites fall silent, and the navigation fleet twenty thousand kilometers up sits at the ring's outer edge, under fire.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring's outer edge touching the navigation shell on the display
shots: MEDIUM, static: Theo watches weather map screens flicker to grey, one after another.
ECU, macro: a phone on the console shows a spinning location marker that never locks.
CU, low angle: Theo's reflection in the dark screen as more dots wink out.
WIDE, slow push-in: the wall display, a second shell of satellites sitting right at the ring's outer edge, sparks flickering across it.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Theo sets the phone face down, the display holding.

blocks.vo_line: Geostationary satellites near thirty six thousand kilometers stay safe, but every rocket that serves them must punch through the ring to get there.
blocks.through_line_state: a thin edge-on ring line above the pad, pierced by a rocket
shots: WIDE, static: a snowy launch pad at high latitude, a rocket standing tall, the ring a thin edge-on line near the horizon.
CU, slow push-in: Theo in a parka checks a handheld gauge and gives a thumbs up.
MEDIUM, low angle: the rocket's engines ignite with a roar and it lifts, snow blasting outward.
ECU, macro: the rocket's nose pierces the thin ring line, grains scattering off it.
WIDE, gentle drift: the exhaust trail bends steeply past the ring, a tiny satellite dot separating high above, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Rings never last, so as the inner edge brushes the atmosphere the grains burn as shooting stars, every night for millions of years.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring shedding bright streaks over a tropical city
shots: WIDE, static: a tropical city plaza at night, palm trees, a crowd, the ring overhead shedding bright streaks.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia among the crowd, every face tipped up.
ECU, macro: a streak flares, splits, and fades in one breath.
CU, slow push-in: Nia counts streaks on her fingers and gives up, laughing.
WIDE, gentle drift: dozens of streaks at once over the plaza, the crowd's shadows shifting with each flash, holds.

blocks.vo_line: Our Moon sits four hundred thousand kilometers away, beyond that boundary, but four and a half billion years ago it was a ring.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring worn thin beside a bright rising Moon
shots: CU, static: a large rock lands on the lawn with a thud beside Nia's chair, smoking.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia backs away, then looks past the thin ring to the rising Moon.
ECU, macro: the Moon's craters, calm and grey, filling the telescope eyepiece view.
WIDE, gentle drift: the backyard with the dashed boundary circle drawn faintly in the sky, the Moon far outside it.
CU, slow push-in: Nia's hand rests on the telescope, her eyes on the Moon, holds.

blocks.vo_line: A Mars sized body struck the young Earth, the debris spread into a disk that pulled itself into the Moon you see tonight.
blocks.through_line_state: the ring disk gathering itself into the Moon, Earth left ringless
shots: MEDIUM, static: a Mars sized body slams into the young glowing Earth with a silent flash.
WIDE, lateral drift: molten debris sprays out and wraps into a glowing disk around the planet.
ECU, macro: glowing droplets clump together, one then another, snapping into a ball.
CU, slow push-in: the disk thins to nothing as the ball rounds off into the Moon.
WIDE, gentle drift: modern Earth with no ring, the full Moon rising beside it, holds still.
